headword: {良薬|りょうやく}{口|くち}に{苦|にが}し
reading: りょうやくくちににがし

definitions.gloss: good medicine tastes bitter; honest advice is hard to hear
definitions.explanation: Beneficial medicine is often unpleasant to take, just as truthful advice or constructive criticism can be difficult to accept. What helps us the most may not be comfortable.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、{良薬|りょうやく}{口|くち}に{苦|にが}し⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The teacher's words are harsh, but good medicine tastes bitter.

examples.japanese: {良薬|りょうやく}{口|くち}に{苦|にが}し⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}って→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{貴重|きちょう}→貴重：00223_kichou⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: As the saying goes, good medicine is bitter—a friend who tells you the truth is precious.

examples.japanese: {良薬|りょうやく}{口|くち}に{苦|にが}し⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{指摘|してき}→指摘：05630_shiteki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{素直|すなお}→素直：00391_sunao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}こう→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: As they say, good medicine tastes bitter, so I'll accept his harsh criticism openly.

notes:
ORIGIN: This proverb comes from Chinese (良药苦口), found in classical Chinese texts. It has been used in Japanese for centuries and is well-known.

FULL FORM: The complete version is {良薬|りょうやく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{苦|にが}けれ→苦い：01201_nigai⟧ど⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{病|やまい}→病：13610_yamai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{利|き}⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{忠言|ちゅうげん}→忠言：22768_chuugen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{逆|さから}えど⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{行|おこな}い→行う：01238_okonau⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{利|り}→利：29142_ri⟧あり (Good medicine is bitter to the mouth but helps cure illness; honest advice is unpleasant to the ear but benefits one's conduct).

USAGE: Used when accepting or advising someone to accept constructive criticism, uncomfortable truths, or difficult but beneficial measures. Often quoted when someone receives harsh but fair feedback.

ENGLISH EQUIVALENTS:
- A bitter pill to swallow
- The truth hurts
- Tough love
